Topics · Is the Quran from God?

Do the oldest manuscripts match today's Quran?

Seventh-century parchment, one early text that differs, a study of shared spellings, and what scholars debate.

Part 1 of 3

﴿كَلَّآ إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ١١ فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُۥ١٢ فِى صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ١٣ مَّرْفُوعَةٍ مُّطَهَّرَةٍۭ١٤ بِأَيْدِى سَفَرَةٍ١٥ كِرَامٍۭ بَرَرَةٍ١٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

No! Indeed, they [i.e., these verses] are a reminder; So whoever wills may remember it.[1857] [It is recorded] in honored sheets, Exalted and purified, [Carried] by the hands of messenger-angels, Noble and dutiful.

Translator's notes

[1857] The revelation. Or "Him," i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) .

Quran · Abasa 80:11-16

Ask the simplest question first: do very old copies exist, and can they be dated? Yes to both, within limits. Some are on parchment, and parchment can be tested for age. The test dates the animal, not the writing, and gives a range, not a year. So the honest answer is a range with a caution. And whatever the range, it is a window you can look through yourself, because these manuscripts are published.

A question for you

How should a range of dates be used?

If you sayAs a window, not a point.
ThenThat is how the scholars use it, and why the honest answer carries a caution.
If you sayAs a reason to check other evidence too, like script and spelling.
ThenYes. Scholars of handwriting and spelling do exactly that, and their disagreements are public.
If you sayI do not trust dating methods.
ThenUnderstandable. That is why the method is checked against handwriting and spelling, and why some scholars doubt single dates.

Part 2 of 3

﴿رَسُولٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ يَتْلُوا۟ صُحُفًا مُّطَهَّرَةً٢ فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ٣﴾

Translation of the meaning

A Messenger from Allāh, reciting purified[1959] scriptures Within which are correct writings [i.e., rulings and laws].

Translator's notes

[1959] i.e., containing no falsehood.

Quran · Al-Bayyinah 98:2-3

One manuscript does visibly differ. At Sanaa, a parchment was written, erased, and written over. The upper text matches the standard text. The lower, earlier text is still the Quran: the same suras, almost the same order of verses, but with some differences of wording and a different order of suras. So variation existed early. And you can see its kind: words and phrases, not a different book.

A question for you

What would you make of an early copy that differs in some words?

If you sayIt shows the text was not frozen at first.
ThenSome read it so. Specialists differ on what this copy was, and its differences stay within words, phrases and sura order, not a different book.
If you sayIt shows a different tradition existed beside the standard one.
ThenSome scholars say so. Others see an early edition or a school copy. This is one of the open questions.
If you sayIt is a small difference. The book is recognisably the same.
ThenThat is close to what the specialists describe, though they do not all draw the same conclusion from it.

Part 3 of 3

﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا ٱلذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُۥ لَحَـٰفِظُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, it is We who sent down the message [i.e., the Qur’ān], and indeed, We will be its guardian.

Quran · Al-Hijr 15:9

Now look the other way. If the standard text came from one early written source, copies descended from it should share its oddities, the way students copying one teacher share his strange spellings. A study in 2019 looked for exactly that in early manuscripts, and found it. Specialists still discuss exactly when the standard written copy was fixed. The tradition places it under Uthman, about 650, and most place it within decades of the Prophet, not centuries.

A question for you

What would you need to see before saying the text was settled early?

If you sayCopies from the earliest years that agree with each other.
ThenThat is what the scholars look for, and the shared spellings are the kind of agreement they mean.
If you sayAgreement among experts who disagree on other things.
ThenMany experts with very different views agree that the text goes back to the seventh century. They differ about the decades after about 650.
If you sayMore than manuscripts: I would need to know the source was divine.
ThenManuscripts cannot show that, and this Step does not claim they do. They speak to how the text was kept, not where it came from.

Your reflection

What do you most want to see with your own eyes before trusting a historical claim: the original, a copy, or the people who studied it?
